meta.title: Vietnamese Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 542 expressions · 181 everyday, 313 idioms, 48 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 542 Vietnamese set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 181 everyday phrases, 313 idioms and 48 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Vietnamese → English (see the Vietnamese, recall the meaning) and English → Vietnamese (see an English meaning, recall the Vietnamese) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Vietnamese A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases or interjections and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas (không có gì, để cho, thể nào …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words', most of them the four-syllable set phrases (thành ngữ) Vietnamese is rich in (khát nước, cắm sừng, đánh trống lảng …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (bán anh em xa mua láng giềng gần, có công mài sắt có ngày nên kim, hổ phụ sinh hổ tử …), a few of which are idioms by another name. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Vietnamese sentences contain them; only 49 of the 542 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how often they occur in film and television subtitles, divided into words against the dictionary. Beneath every expression its tones are named, one per syllable. Real example sentences come with 49 of the 542 expressions, three apiece for 13, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, pronunciation and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then the OpenSubtitles 2018 Vietnamese text (opensubtitles.org, via the OPUS corpus collection), counted here. Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
